DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 93-b s. 2022 15 September 2022 HON. ANTONINO M. JUMAWID Mayor Municipality of Batuan, Province of Bohol Dear Mayor Jumawid: This has reference to the letter dated 27 July 2022 of G.D. Anino & Associates, on behalf of its client, Ms. Librada Tirol-Dumagan, in relation to her request for legal assistance and opinion on the reopening of Ri-Ia-Ye Cockpit Arena, in the Municipality of Batuan, Province of Bohol. In your letter, you stated that according to your client, Ms. Librada Tirol-Dumagan (Ms. Librada), the Ri-Ia-Ye Cockpit Arena (Ri-la-Ya) was not operational since 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Subsequently, in the past months, the province of Bohol was declared under Alert Level I. Correspondingly, cockpit arenas in other municipalities of the province have reopened for the gaming public and resumed its operations. However, for the Municipality of Batuan, despite repeated requests to allow the opening of Ri-Ia-Ya, Ms. Librada alleges that you have continued to deny such requests. In addition, even though the Balilihan Cockpit Arena, which you are managing, according to Ms. Librada, is now operational. Under this premise arose the request for legal assistance and the appropriate action concerning the reopening of Ri-la-Ye. At the outset, we deem it proper to highlight that this Department has issued Memorandum Circular No. 2022-003 ("MC No. 2022-003") dated 19 January 2022, pursuant to Resolution No. 154, series of 2021 issued by the Inter-Agency Task Force for the Management of Emerging and Infectious Diseases (IATF-MElD)dated 14 December 2021, allowing for the operation of cockpits and traditional cockfighting in areas under Alert Level 2, enjoining all concerned local government units (LGUs) to undertake the necessary actions in the management of cockpits and the conduct of cockfighting activites placed under Alert Level 2 or lower. Accordingly, under MC No. 2022-003, LGUs, exercising sound judgment, and in compliance to the guidelines by the National Government, shall have the discretion in allowing operations of licensed cockpits, as well as the conduct of cockfighting activities within their area of jurisdiction. Thus, operations of cockpits and traditional cockfighting may be allowed in areas under Alert Level 2 or lower provided that there should be no objection from the concerned LGUs, and shall be subject to strict observance of the following specific protocols: "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

I. 2. 3. 4. Maximum of fifty percent (50%) venue capacity for fully vaccinated individuals only; All on-site workers/employees of these establishments are fully vaccinated against COVID-19; Betting shall be cashless and shall use technology-based platforms only, no physical exchange of cash anywhere in the cockpit and no oral placing of bets; Minimum public health standards (MPHS) shall be strictly observed in areas where traditional cockfighting is conducted, which include proper wearing of face masks and strict enforcement of no face mask, no entry policy; physical distancing of at least one meter and hand hygiene (alcohols/hand sanitizers/disinfecting materials) should be made available for all patrons, employees and visitors. However, it is imperative to emphasize that, notwithstanding the fact that the LGUs shall have the authority and discretion regarding the resumption of the operations of licensed cockpits and cock fighting activities, we would like to remind you that this power is not unlimited, and shall not in any way be exercised capriciously and whimsically or in an arbitrary and despotic manner. Please be guided accordingly. Very truly yours, BY THE AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: GAN n erse tary for Local Government OSEC/BCA/LLLS-LRALLD/rjki COPY FURNISHED: LEOCADIO T.
